properties.headline: The Great Sarawak Kolo Mee Trail
properties.text: A (completely fictional) culinary expedition across Borneo in search of the perfect bowl of kolo mee. Five towns, five legends, zero calories counted. Buckle up — the noodles are calling.
properties.caption: Warning: contains dramatised noodle facts.

properties.headline: Kuching — The Origin Bowl
properties.text: Legend says the very first bowl of kolo mee was tossed here at 3:47 a.m. by a cat who refused to sleep. Locals still leave out a saucer of char siu in tribute. The city's stray cats are rumoured to review hawker stalls with a strict five-whisker rating system.
properties.caption: Cat City. Coincidence? The felines think not.
properties.name: Kuching

properties.headline: Mukah — The Sago Detour
properties.text: Our expedition briefly abandons noodles for umai and sago pearls. Scientists (imaginary ones) estimate that Mukah produces enough sago each year to build a bouncy castle the size of a small island. No one has tried. Yet.
properties.caption: Sago: chewy, wobbly, structurally underrated.
properties.name: Mukah

properties.headline: Sibu — The Kampua Rivalry
properties.text: Here the trail turns tense. Sibu insists its kampua mee is the true champion, not kolo mee. Diplomatic noodle summits are held nightly at the pasar. So far, the only treaty signed is that everyone orders a second bowl.
properties.caption: Neutral ground: the shared chilli sauce bottle.
properties.name: Sibu

properties.headline: Bintulu — Refuel at the Energy Town
properties.text: Powered by natural gas and, apparently, unlimited belacan, Bintulu is where our travellers refuel — both the van and themselves. Local myth claims a bowl of noodles here gives you enough energy to walk to Miri. It does not. We checked.
properties.caption: Fuel gauge: full. Stomach gauge: fuller.
properties.name: Bintulu

properties.headline: Miri — The Final Bowl
properties.text: The trail ends where it began, in oil-town Miri, with a sunset, a seahorse mascot, and the biggest bowl of kolo mee anyone dared to order. Verdict after 1,200 km: they are all the best. This is the only scientifically imaginary conclusion possible.
properties.caption: The Seahorse City approves this expedition.
properties.name: Miri
